Rashi on Eruvin 36a:10:1.hebrew: נדמעו - חולין הוו מעיקרא מתוקנין, ונפלה בהן תרומה ונדמעו. והאי תנא סבר לה כסומכוס דאמר (לעיל עירובין דף כו:): אין מערבין לישראל בתרומה. הלכך, אם מבע"י נדמעו, אע"ג דחזי לכהנים — אין עירובו עירוב. ל"א: נדמעו — שנפל לתוכן טבל, דלא חזי אפילו לכהן:
Rashi on Eruvin 36a:10:1.english: They became mixed - They were originally properly prepared non-sacred food, and terumah fell into them and they became mixed. And this tanna holds in accordance with Sumakhos, who said (above, 26b): One may not establish an eiruv for an Israelite with terumah. Therefore, if they became mixed while it was still day, even though it is fit for priests, his eiruv is not a [valid] eiruv. Another explanation: "They became mixed" — that untithed produce [tevel] fell into them, which is not fit even for a priest.

Rashi on Eruvin 36a:11:1.hebrew: עירבו לי בטהורה בכל מקום שהיא - והניחום שתיהן יחד בסוף התחום. ובככרות של תרומה עסקינן, דאי בחולין — חולין טמאין מותרין הן, דלאו כל אדם אוכל חוליו בטהרה:
Rashi on Eruvin 36a:11:1.english: Establish an eiruv for me with the pure [loaf], wherever it is - And they placed both of them together at the end of the [Shabbat] boundary. And we are dealing with loaves of teruma, for if [they were loaves] of non-sacred food, impure non-sacred food is permitted, as not every person eats his non-sacred food in purity.

Rashi on Eruvin 36a:12:1.hebrew: דליכא טהורה - ודאית, דשמא מבעוד יום נטמאת:
Rashi on Eruvin 36a:12:1.english: Where there is no pure [loaf] - A definitely [pure one], for perhaps it became defiled while it was still day.

Rashi on Eruvin 36a:12:2.hebrew: או דילמא אפילו ר' יוסי - לא מכשר במתני' אלא משום דאי טהורה היא — הא ידע לה היכא היא ואיזו היא סעודתו, ומשום ספק טומאה לא מיפסלא — דאמר: אוקמא אחזקה:
Rashi on Eruvin 36a:12:2.english: Or perhaps even Rabbi Yosei - does not validate [the eiruv] in the Mishnah except because if it is pure, behold, he knows where it is and which is his meal; and on account of the uncertainty regarding ritual impurity it is not disqualified, for he says: "Establish it on its status quo."

Rashi on Eruvin 36a:12:3.english: But here, he does not know - Which one is his meal.

Rashi on Eruvin 36a:13:1.hebrew: בעינן סעודה הראויה מבע"י וליכא - ואין עירובו כלום, דאפילו חמר גמל לא הוי; דבשלמא מתני' — סעודה הראויה הואי, והשתא הוא דאיתיליד בה ספק:
Rashi on Eruvin 36a:13:1.english: We require a meal that is fit while it is still day, and there is none - And his eiruv is nothing, for it is not even a case of a donkey driver and a camel driver; for granted, in the Mishnah it was a fit meal, and it is only now that a doubt arose concerning it.

Rashi on Eruvin 36a:14:1.hebrew: ככר זו כו' - אמר על ככר אחת בע"ש: "היום יהא חול, ולמחר יהא קדש", ועירב שלוחו בה:
Rashi on Eruvin 36a:14:1.english: This loaf, etc. - He said regarding one loaf on Shabbat eve: “Today it shall be unconsecrated, and tomorrow it shall be consecrated,” and his agent established an eiruv with it.

Rashi on Eruvin 36a:14:2.hebrew: מהו - הואיל ובין השמשות ספק הוא, חיישינן דילמא קודם קניית עירוב חל עליה הקדש, ואין מערבין בהקדש, או לא אמרינן הכי:
Rashi on Eruvin 36a:14:2.english: What is [the halakha]? - Since twilight is [a period of] uncertainty, do we suspect that perhaps before the acquisition of the eiruv, consecration took effect upon it — and one may not establish an eiruv with consecrated property — or do we not say this?

Rashi on Eruvin 36a:15:1.hebrew: היום תהא קודש ולמחר תהא חול - על מעות שיש לי בבית. מהו? מי אמרינן: כי מטא בין השמשות, נפק ליה מקדושתיה וקנה עירוב, או לא:
Rashi on Eruvin 36a:15:1.english: Today it shall be consecrated and tomorrow it shall be unconsecrated - [i.e., it shall be redeemed] onto money that I have in my house. What is [the halakha]? Do we say: When twilight arrives, it departs from its sanctity and establishes the eiruv, or not?

Rashi on Eruvin 36a:15:2.hebrew: ומאי שנא - הא בין השמשות ספיקא הוא, מאי שנא הכא לקולא והכא לחומרא:
Rashi on Eruvin 36a:15:2.english: And what is different - Behold, twilight is an uncertainty; what is different [such that] here [we rule] leniently and here stringently?

Rashi on Eruvin 36a:16:1.hebrew: לכי תיכול עלה כורא דמילחא - לכשתמדוד כור של מלח על דבר זה ותתנהו לי, אומר לך טעמו:
Rashi on Eruvin 36a:16:1.english: When you measure a kor of salt for it - When you measure a kor of salt for this matter and give it to me, I will tell you its reason:

Rashi on Eruvin 36a:16:2.hebrew: היום חול ולמחר קודש - ובין השמשות דקניית עירוב ספיקא הוא, ומספיקא לא תפקיה ממילתיה קמייתא. וכן סיפא:
Rashi on Eruvin 36a:16:2.english: Today [it is] unconsecrated and tomorrow consecrated - And twilight, [the time] of the acquisition of the eiruv, is [a matter of] doubt, and out of doubt you do not remove it from its initial status. And so too [in] the latter clause.

Rashi on Eruvin 36a:17:1.hebrew: של מעשר - ראשון, שהיה עדיין טבל, שלא הפריש הלוי ממנה תרומת מעשר. והרי הוא במיתה בעודו טבל — ואפילו לכהנים — ולא חזי לעירוב. ולגבי לגין טבול יום: בעודו טבל לא פסיל, דטבול יום מותר בנגיעה לחולין ולמעשר, ואע"ג דפתיכא ביה תרומה שלא הורמה. ואמר: הרי זו שבלגין תרומת מעשר על החבית לכשתחשך, ויעריב שמשו, שתהא כשרה לתרומה:
Rashi on Eruvin 36a:17:1.english: Of tithe - First [tithe], which was still tevel, as the Levite had not yet separated terumat ma’aser from it. And behold, [eating] it is punishable by death while it is tevel — even for priests — and it is not fit for an eiruv. And with regard to the flask of a tevul yom: while [the produce] is still tevel, [the flask] does not disqualify it, because a tevul yom is permitted to touch non-sacred produce and [first] tithe, even though unseparated teruma is mixed in it. And he said: “Let this [produce] in the flask be terumat ma’aser for the barrel when it gets dark,” and [by then] its sun will have set, so that it will be fit for teruma.

Rashi on Eruvin 36a:17:2.english: His statement takes effect - And the teruma is pure.

Rashi on Eruvin 36a:18:1.hebrew: ואם אמר עירבו לי בלגין זה לא אמר כלום - הואיל וכי מטא בין השמשות, אכתי טבל הוה:
Rashi on Eruvin 36a:18:1.english: And if he said: Establish an eiruv for me with this flask, he has not said anything - Since when twilight arrived, it was still tevel.

Rashi on Eruvin 36a:18:2.hebrew: סוף היום - תחילת בין השמשות, שהוא סוף היום של ע"ש:
Rashi on Eruvin 36a:18:2.english: The end of the day - The beginning of twilight, which is the end of the day of Shabbat eve.

Rashi on Eruvin 36a:18:3.english: The eiruv acquires [residence] - And at the end of the day, it is still tevel.

Rashi on Eruvin 36a:1:1.hebrew: רבא אמר - גבי נגע באחד נמי, אפילו יש שני כיתי עדים חלוקות — אחת אומרת: קודם שנגע בו מת, ואחת אומרת: עכשיו מת — הוי נמי ר"מ מטהר, ואפילו הכי לא תיקשי:
Rashi on Eruvin 36a:1:1.english: Rava said - In the case of [one who] touched someone as well, even if there are two conflicting sets of witnesses, [where] one says, “He died before he touched him,” and one says, “He died just now,” Rabbi Meir would also rule [him] pure; and even so, it is not difficult.

Rashi on Eruvin 36a:1:2.hebrew: התם תרי חזקי נינהו - לטהר, ומשום הכי אזלינן לקולא — דאוקי תרי לבהדי תרי, והעמד מת על חזקתו ראשונה כל הלילה וחי הוה, ועוד: העמד נוגע על חזקתו ראשונה וטהור היה:
Rashi on Eruvin 36a:1:2.english: There, they are two presumptions - to rule [him] pure, and because of this we follow the lenient ruling: For set two [witnesses] against two [witnesses], and establish the dead person upon his initial presumption throughout the night, that he was alive; and furthermore, establish the one who touched [him] upon his initial presumption, that he was pure.

Rashi on Eruvin 36a:1:3.hebrew: הכא - במתניתין, חדא חזקה הוא דאיכא למימר: "העמד תרומה על חזקתה". ומשום חדא חזקה לא מרעינן סהדי, הלכך אזלינן לחומרא:
Rashi on Eruvin 36a:1:3.english: Here - In our Mishnah, there is [only] one presumption that can be stated: "Establish the teruma on its presumptive status." And on account of [only] one presumption we do not undermine [the testimony of] witnesses; therefore, we follow the stringent [ruling].

Rashi on Eruvin 36a:2:1.hebrew: קשיא דר' יוסי - דברייתא דקתני: בספק טבל ובספק לא טבל, ובטומאה דרבנן — אכל אוכלין כו' — ורבי יוסי מטמא; ומתני' קתני: ספק עירוב כשר. ואפילו תחומין דרבנן — תיקשי:
Rashi on Eruvin 36a:2:1.english: A contradiction [between the statements] of Rabbi Yosei - For the baraita teaches: [In a case of] doubt whether one immersed or doubt whether one did not immerse, and regarding rabbinic impurity — [such as where one] ate [impure] foods, etc. — Rabbi Yosei renders [him] impure; and our mishna teaches: [An eiruv whose validity is in] doubt is valid. And even [if] Shabbat boundaries are rabbinic — it is [still] difficult.

Rashi on Eruvin 36a:3:1.hebrew: הואיל ויש לה עיקר מן התורה - דיש טומאה מן התורה, ויש להחמיר בספק טבילתה — להכי אחמור רבנן אף בספק טבילת טומאה דרבנן, דלא ליתי לזלזולי בספק טבילת טומאה דאורייתא:
Rashi on Eruvin 36a:3:1.english: Since it has a basis in the Torah - For there is impurity by Torah law, and one must be stringent in [a case of] uncertainty regarding its immersion; therefore, the Rabbis were stringent even in [a case of] uncertainty regarding immersion for rabbinic impurity, so that one does not come to treat lightly [a case of] uncertainty regarding immersion for Torah impurity.

Rashi on Eruvin 36a:3:2.hebrew: שבת נמי דאורייתא היא - אתחומין פריך, למימר דתחומין דאורייתא, וכר' עקיבא במס' סוטה (דף ל:):
Rashi on Eruvin 36a:3:2.english: Shabbat is also by Torah law - [The Gemara] poses its objection regarding [Shabbat] limits, meaning to say that [Shabbat] limits are by Torah law, and in accordance with Rabbi Akiva in Tractate Sotah (daf 30b).

Rashi on Eruvin 36a:3:3.hebrew: ומשני קסבר רבי יוסי תחומין דרבנן - ומשום דלא ליתו לזלזולי בשאר ספיקות דמלאכת שבת, ליכא למיגזר — דלא דמו מלאכות לתחומין, אבל טומאות דמו להדדי:
Rashi on Eruvin 36a:3:3.english: And [the Gemara] answers: Rabbi Yosei holds [that Shabbat] limits are rabbinic - And [as for the concern] that they might come to treat other doubts regarding the creative labors of Shabbat lightly, there is no [need] to issue a decree, as creative labors do not resemble [Shabbat] limits; but [all forms of] ritual impurity resemble one another.

Rashi on Eruvin 36a:4:1.hebrew: דידיה - מחמיר אפילו בספק דרבנן, ומתניתין דרביה אבטולמוס היא:
Rashi on Eruvin 36a:4:1.english: His [own view] - He is stringent even regarding a rabbinic doubt, and our Mishnah is [the view of] his teacher, Avtolemos.

Rashi on Eruvin 36a:5:1.hebrew: העמד טמא על חזקתו - כוליה חזקה לחומרא איכא, לקולא ליכא. אבל מתניתין — איכא חזקה לקולא ולחומרא: העמד אדם על חזקת תחום ביתו, ואמר: לא עירב; העמד תרומה על חזקתה, ועירב; ובדרבנן — לקולא אזלינן:
Rashi on Eruvin 36a:5:1.english: Keep the impure [person] in his presumptive state - The entire presumption is for stringency; there is none for leniency. But [in] our Mishnah, there is a presumption for leniency and [a presumption] for stringency: Establish a person in the presumptive status of his home's [Shabbat] boundary, and say: He did not establish an eruv; establish the terumah in its presumptive status, and [say that] he did establish an eruv; and in [matters of] rabbinic law, we follow the lenient [course].

Rashi on Eruvin 36a:6:1.english: That had not been measured - From its inception, and [thus] it had not stood in a presumption of fitness.

Rashi on Eruvin 36a:7:1.english: [If] one established an eiruv with terumah - [That was] ritually pure, and it became impure after he placed it there.

Rashi on Eruvin 36a:7:2.hebrew: ספק מבעוד יום נטמאת ספק משחשיכה נטמאת - אמרינן: אוקמיה בין השמשות אחזקת' קמייתא, וטהורה הואי; והשתא משחשיכה הוא דאיטמי:
Rashi on Eruvin 36a:7:2.english: [There is] doubt whether it became impure while it was still day, [or] doubt whether it became impure after nightfall - We say: Establish it at twilight upon its initial presumption, and it was pure; and [it was only] now, after nightfall, that it became impure.

Rashi on Eruvin 36a:7:3.english: And similarly with produce - Of untithed produce [tevel].

Rashi on Eruvin 36a:7:4.english: [There is a] doubt whether they were rendered fit while it was still day - After he placed them there.

Rashi on Eruvin 36a:7:5.hebrew: ספק משחשיכה נתקנו - ולא קנה עירוב, כדתנן במתני': "אבל לא בטבל". ולקמן פריך בהאי: מה חזקת כשרות איכא דמכשר רבי יוסי? דהא איכא למימר: העמד טבל על חזקתו:
Rashi on Eruvin 36a:7:5.english: [Or] doubt whether they were rendered fit after nightfall - and [in that case] he would not acquire an eiruv, as we learned in the Mishnah: “But not with tevel [untithed produce].” And later, [the Gemara] objects concerning this: What presumption of fitness is there [here] that Rabbi Yosei validates [the eiruv]? For behold, one can say: Maintain the tevel in its presumptive status!

Rashi on Eruvin 36a:8:1.hebrew: ספק טמאה ספק טהורה - דקודם שהניחה שם נולד לה ספק, ולא היה שם חזקת הכשר עירוב מעולם:
Rashi on Eruvin 36a:8:1.english: [There was] doubt [whether it was] impure [or] doubt [whether it was] pure - For before he placed it there, a doubt arose regarding it, and there was never a presumption of validity for an eiruv there.

Rashi on Eruvin 36a:9:1.hebrew: מאי שנא תרומה - דרישא — ספק מבעוד יום ניטמא, ספק משחשיכה — דמכשר ר' יוסי משום חזקה קמייתא:
Rashi on Eruvin 36a:9:1.english: What is different about teruma - [The case] of the opening clause — [where there is] doubt whether it became impure while it was still day, [or] doubt whether after nightfall — which Rabbi Yosei validates on account of the initial presumption.

Rashi on Eruvin 36a:9:2.hebrew: פירות - ספק מבעוד יום נתקנו, ספק משחשיכה — נוקמינהו נמי אחזקה קמייתא דטבל הוו, וליפסול:
Rashi on Eruvin 36a:9:2.english: Produce - [Where there is] uncertainty [whether] they were rendered fit while it was still day, [or] uncertainty [whether] after nightfall — let us also establish them upon their original presumptive state, that they were untithed produce [tevel], and let [the eruv] be invalid!

Tosafot on Eruvin 36a:10:1.hebrew: ספק נדמעו - נראה כפ"ה בלשון שני: נדמעו — טבל בחולין, ולא כסתם דימוע שבהש"ס. אבל לשון ראשון, שפירש: נדמעו — תרומה בחולין, ואתיא כסומכוס — אין נראה; דהא קתני בברייתא דמערבין בתרומה, ודוחק לומר דמיירי בתרומה לכהן:
Tosafot on Eruvin 36a:10:1.english: "Doubt whether they became mixed" - It appears in accordance with the explanation of the Kuntres [Rashi] in the second version: "they became mixed" [means that] untithed produce [tevel became mixed] into non-sacred produce [chullin], and not like the standard [meaning of] dimua throughout the Shas [which refers to terumah falling into chullin]. However, the first version, which explained [that] "they became mixed" [means that] terumah [fell] into non-sacred produce, and [that the baraita] follows [the opinion of] Sumakhos — does not appear [correct]; for behold, the baraita teaches that one may establish an eiruv with terumah, and it is forced to say that it is dealing with terumah for a priest.

Tosafot on Eruvin 36a:15:1.hebrew: מאי שנא - ואם תאמר: והא רבא גופיה קאמר בסמוך, "זאת אומרת סוף היום קונה עירוב", ואם סוף היום קונה עירוב — אתיא דרב נחמן שפיר, ואמאי קמיבעיא ליה "מאי שנא"? ויש לומר: דע"כ דרבא אית ליה דתחלת היום קונה עירוב, דהא פסיק בריש ביצה (דף ד:) כרב, דאמר: "נולדה בזה אסורה בזה", וטעמא דרב משום הכנה, ומאן דאית ליה הכנה סבר תחילת היום קונה עירוב, כדמוכח בפירקין (דף לח:); ורבא דאמר "זאת אומרת סוף היום קונה עירוב" — אליבא דברייתא קאמר, וליה לא ס"ל:
Tosafot on Eruvin 36a:15:1.english: What is different - And if you say: But doesn't Rava himself say nearby, "That is to say, the end of the day acquires the eiruv"? And if the end of the day acquires the eiruv, Rav Naḥman's [ruling] works out well; so why did he raise the dilemma, "What is different?" And one can say: Perforce Rava holds that the beginning of the day acquires the eiruv, as he ruled at the beginning of Beitzah (4b) in accordance with Rav, who said: "[An egg that] was laid on this [day] is forbidden on that [day]," and Rav's reason is because of preparation [hakhana], and whoever holds [the reason of] preparation maintains that the beginning of the day acquires the eiruv, as is demonstrated in our chapter (38b). And [as for] Rava saying, "That is to say, the end of the day acquires the eiruv" — he said [it] according to the baraita, but he himself does not hold [this view].

Tosafot on Eruvin 36a:6:1.hebrew: אדרבה העמד מקוה על חזקתו - הוה מצי לשנויי: "הרי חסר לפניך", כדאמר פר' קמא דנדה (דף ב.); אלא דלא מיירי הכא במקוה שנמדד ונמצא חסר:
Tosafot on Eruvin 36a:6:1.english: "On the contrary, keep the ritual bath in its presumptive state" - [The Gemara] could have answered: "Behold, it is lacking before you," as it says in the first chapter of Niddah (2a); rather, [the Gemara] is not dealing here with a ritual bath that was measured and found lacking.

Tosafot on Eruvin 36a:6:2.hebrew: במקוה שלא נמדד - וא"ת: והא רבי יוסי מטמא אפילו טהרות אם נגע בהן, דלענין דאמרינן ליה "זיל טבול", אפילו ר"מ מודה, כדאמרינן גבי ספק טומאה ברשות הרבים; וא"כ, אדרבה, נימא: אוקי טהרות על חזקתן? וי"ל, דבספיקא דרבנן כי הכא, לא אמרינן "זיל טבול" לרבי מאיר, ופליגי אגברא אי בעי טבילה; אבל טהרות — מודה רבי יוסי דלא מטמאינן. וכן איתא במסכת מקואות (פ"ב משנה ב) דקתני: "ורבי יוסי מטמא, שספק ליטמא — טמא, לטמא אחרים — טהור":
Tosafot on Eruvin 36a:6:2.english: In a ritual bath that had not been measured - And if you say: But doesn't Rabbi Yosei render even teharot [ritually pure items] impure if he touched them? For with regard to telling him, "Go immerse," even Rabbi Meir agrees, as we say regarding a doubt of ritual impurity in the public domain. And if so, on the contrary, let us say: Keep the teharot in their presumptive state [of purity]! And one can say that in a rabbinic doubt such as this, we do not say "Go immerse" according to Rabbi Meir, and they disagree about the person [himself], whether he requires immersion; but [regarding] teharot, Rabbi Yosei agrees that we do not render [them] impure. And so it is in tractate Mikvaot (chapter 2, mishna 2), which teaches: "And Rabbi Yosei renders [him] impure, for [in a case of] a doubt regarding becoming impure, [he is] impure; [but regarding] rendering others impure, [he is] pure."

Tosafot on Eruvin 36a:8:1.hebrew: אבל עירב בתרומה ספק טמאה ספק טהורה - כגון שהיו ב' ציבורין לפניו: אחד היה תרומה טמאה ואחד היה תרומה טהורה, ועירב באחד מהן — דליכא חזקה כלל:
Tosafot on Eruvin 36a:8:1.english: "However, if one established an eiruv with teruma [about which there was] doubt whether it was impure or pure" - For example, where there were two piles before him: one was impure teruma and one was pure teruma, and he established an eiruv with one of them — as there is no presumption [of purity] at all.
